cards.explanation: The answer is divorcing a wife for any reason. The Pharisees ask, "Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?" (Matthew 19:3). Pharisees were a strict religious group, and Matthew says they came to test Him. So this question came as a test, friends.

The answer is when the Creator made them male and female. Jesus says, "Have you not read that from the beginning the Creator ‘made them male and female,’" (Matthew 19:4). He doesn't start with a rule, friends. He starts at the beginning. These are people who know their Scriptures, so I think that question lands with a little sting.

The answer is that man should not separate it. Jesus says, "Therefore what God has joined together, let man not separate." (Matthew 19:6). He had just said they are no longer two, but one flesh. The line is short, bakers, and it needs no help from me.

The answer is hardness. Jesus says, "Moses permitted you to divorce your wives because of your hardness of heart." (Matthew 19:8). Notice He says Moses permitted it, friends. He didn't say it was the plan. Then He adds, "But it was not this way from the beginning."

The answer is False. Jesus says, "Moses permitted you to divorce your wives because of your hardness of heart. But it was not this way from the beginning." (Matthew 19:8). So divorce was not the way it was from the beginning, friends. He points them back to how things started, with the Creator making them male and female (Matthew 19:4).

The answer is True. His disciples say, "If this is the case between a man and his wife, it is better not to marry." (Matthew 19:10). I think Jesus's teaching hit them hard, friends. I bet they were stunned, and honestly, I'd have been staring at my apron too.

The answer is the kingdom of heaven. Jesus says some "…live like eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven." (Matthew 19:12). He names three kinds, bakers: those born that way, those made that way by men, and those who live that way for the kingdom. Then He says, "The one who can accept this should accept it."

The answer is let them come and do not hinder them. Jesus says, "Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them!" (Matthew 19:14). The disciples had just rebuked the people bringing the children, friends. Jesus says the opposite, and He says it with an exclamation point.

The answer is such as these children. Jesus says, "For the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these." (Matthew 19:14). That's His reason for not hindering the children, friends. They are the ones He points to.

The answer is True. Matthew says, "And after He had placed His hands on them, He went on from there." (Matthew 19:15). The children were brought for Him to place His hands on them (Matthew 19:13), and He did, bakers. The disciples' scolding didn't get the last word.
